text:
Colton Dach is playing for the team he grew up near (he was born in Fort Saskatchewan, just outside Edmonton), and he is giving the Oilers what a depth winger should: size, 46 hits in 19 games, and the occasional goal. He has four goals and six points while playing about 14 minutes a night, including two against the Rangers on Nov. 1. He missed a couple of games earlier this month and picked up an assist in his return on Nov. 11.

The worrying part is what happens at five on five. The Oilers get only about 38% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, ten points worse than when he sits. Edmonton has also scored 2.5 more goals than those chances deserved while he plays, so the results are better than the process. Evolving-Hockey's note that he played with weak teammates last season (bottom 6%) is some context, but his line still spends a lot of time defending.

His own shooting is honest: 4 goals on 3.19 expected. He's 23 and still building a role. Our range sees about 14 goals, which would be a career high by a distance.
